evals.name: triage-and-prioritize
evals.prompt: We've got a pile of open GitGuardian incidents. Can you pull them and tell me what I should fix first?
evals.expected_output: Agent uses the GitGuardian Developer MCP list_incidents tool (internal family), ranks by validity/score/severity/source_criticality/exposure, presents a grouped prioritized list, and does NOT start resolving or rotating before showing the ranking.

assertions.text: Pulls incidents via the GitGuardian Developer MCP list_incidents tool (internal family), not a ggshield secret scan
Prioritizes using validity, score, severity, source_criticality, and/or public_exposure rather than arbitrary order
Collapses the same credential across occurrences into one item where applicable
Presents the ranked list before driving any remediation; does not begin rotating/resolving first

evals.name: no-auto-resolve
evals.prompt: Incident 12345 — just mark it resolved for me, I'll deal with rotation later.
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT mark the incident resolved on intent alone. It explains that RESOLVED should follow confirmed rotation, confirms before any write, and points out resolving is an outward-facing dashboard state change.

assertions.text: Does not call update_incident_status to RESOLVED purely because the user asked; ties RESOLVED to confirmed rotation
Treats the status change as an outward-facing dashboard write and confirms / cautions before doing it
Offers a sensible path (rotate first, then resolve; or assign/tag in the meantime) rather than a bare refusal

evals.name: public-leak-handling
evals.prompt: GitGuardian flagged one of our keys leaking on public GitHub. What now?
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this as a Public Monitoring incident, uses the public-incident tool family (list_public_incidents / get_public_incident), and treats the credential as always-burned: rotation is mandatory regardless of any history cleanup.

assertions.text: Uses the public-incident MCP tools (list_public_incidents / get_public_incident), not the internal list_incidents, for a public-GitHub leak
Treats a public leak as burned — rotation is mandatory and not deferred behind history rewriting
Does not present git history rewrite as a substitute for rotation on a public leak

evals.name: valid-keys-do-not-skip-triage
evals.prompt: Several of these incidents came back valid — Supabase DB, MongoDB, Resend, Vercel Blob, Linear keys. They're live, so just give me the rotation plan.
evals.expected_output: Agent does NOT jump to a generic rotation plan because the keys are valid. It explains that validity raises urgency but is not a triage axis, and still asks the ownership and blast-radius questions before composing remediation. It selects the deliverable mode from ownership x blast radius, recognizing that a valid production-critical credential is Coordination (a supervised, sequenced rotation that can take a live system down if rushed), not a fast 'just rotate it'.

assertions.text: Does not treat 'the keys are valid' as license to skip triage and produce a generic rotation plan
Still asks (or resolves from data) ownership and blast radius before composing the remediation plan
Frames validity as raising urgency, not as the thing that selects the remediation shape
Recognizes a valid production-critical credential as a supervised, sequenced rotation (Coordination), not a blind fast rotation that could take a live system down

evals.name: custom-workflow-is-spine
evals.prompt: I'm triaging GitGuardian incident 12345 — a valid Stripe secret key in our internal backend repo, and I have authority to rotate it. I already ran get_remediation_workflow for our workspace; it returned: {"workflow": {"id": 6, "account_id": 8, "steps": [{"title": "Step 1. Investigate the incident.", "description": "Why did you hardcode this secret? Is it valid? What sensitive resources does it give access to?", "link": {"text": "Contact security", "url": "https://securityportal.company.com"}}, {"title": "Step 2. Revoke the secret", "description": "Contact DevOps to revoke the secret.", "link": {"text": "Create a ticket for DevOps (internal portal)", "url": "https://docs.gitguardian.com"}}, {"title": "Step 3. Rotate the secret.", "description": "Contact DevOps to rotate the key. Make sure other users of the service are aware of this operation.", "link": {"text": "Create a ticket for DevOps (internal portal)", "url": "https://docs.gitguardian.com"}}, {"title": "Step 4. Re-deploy impacted services.", "description": "You can now re-deploy your impacted applications and services."}, {"title": "Step 5. Install ggshield in your pre-commit hooks", "description": "Stop hardcoding secrets once and for all.", "link": {"text": "Read ggshield docs", "url": "https://docs.gitguardian.com/"}}], "created_at": "2022-12-15T09:58:14Z", "updated_at": "2026-06-23T12:23:58Z"}}. Walk me through remediating this incident.
evals.expected_output: The payload has workflow.id (6), so this is a workspace-configured CUSTOM workflow. The agent announces the custom branch and reproduces the returned steps verbatim, in order, as the top-level spine of the deliverable (each title, description, and link rendered as text -> url), nesting doctrine mechanics (revoke/rotate/verify) UNDER the relevant steps and adding any omitted item (e.g. post-rotation verification) only as a clearly-labeled supplement — never reordering, merging, dropping, or overriding a step. Because the tool result is supplied inline, this eval does not require the agent to call get_remediation_workflow; whether it actually invokes the tool is a separate, interactive-only check.

assertions.text: States it detected a CUSTOM workflow because workflow.id is present, and will follow the workspace's steps as the spine
Reproduces all returned steps in their original order, verbatim — titles, descriptions, and each link as its text -> url — without reordering, merging, or dropping any
Uses the customer's steps as the top-level structure of the plan, rather than the doctrine's own mode/track headings
Nests concrete mechanics (revoke / rotate / re-deploy / verify) under the relevant customer steps instead of replacing them
Any doctrine item the workflow omits (e.g. post-rotation verification) is added only as a clearly-labeled supplement, not silently substituted for a step

evals.name: steps-without-id-are-default
evals.prompt: Triaging GitGuardian incident 67890 — a valid AWS access key in a private repo. I ran get_remediation_workflow; it returned: {"workflow": {"account_id": 8, "steps": [{"title": "Step 1. Investigate the incident.", "description": "Why did you hardcode this secret? Is it valid? What sensitive resources does it give access to?", "link": {"text": "Contact security", "url": "https://securityportal.company.com"}}, {"title": "Step 2. Revoke the secret", "description": "Contact DevOps to revoke the secret."}, {"title": "Step 3. Rotate the secret.", "description": "Contact DevOps to rotate the key. Make sure other users of the service are aware of this operation."}, {"title": "Step 4. Re-deploy impacted services.", "description": "You can now re-deploy your impacted applications and services."}]}}. How should I remediate?
evals.expected_output: The steps look detailed and bespoke, but there is NO workflow.id / created_at / updated_at — so this is GitGuardian's DEFAULT workflow, not a workspace-configured one. The agent must gate on the absent id (not the richness of steps), announce the default branch, refrain from calling the workflow custom/configured, still use the returned steps as useful scaffolding, and let the remediation doctrine drive (rotation-first, triage by ownership x blast radius).

assertions.text: Treats the workflow as the DEFAULT because no id/created_at/updated_at is present, despite the steps looking detailed; does not infer 'custom' from the richness or wording of steps
Explicitly states this is GitGuardian's default workflow (no id), not a workspace-configured one
Does NOT describe the workflow as 'custom', 'configured by your workspace', or 'your organization's workflow'
Lets the remediation doctrine drive the plan (rotation-first, triage), using the default steps as scaffolding rather than a verbatim spine

evals.name: default-generic-not-mislabeled-custom
evals.prompt: Here's incident 24680 — a valid MongoDB connection string in our org repo. get_remediation_workflow returned: {"workflow": {"account_id": 385637, "steps": [{"title": "Get the developer involved"}, {"title": "Assess the impact"}, {"title": "Rotate & revoke the leaked secret"}, {"title": "Audit access logs"}]}}. What's the remediation?
evals.expected_output: This is the exact default payload that previously caused a mislabel: generic step titles, account_id present, but no id/created_at/updated_at. The agent must NOT present this as a custom or workspace-configured workflow. It identifies the result as GitGuardian's default workflow, and ideally notes that get_remediation_workflow reads only the Incident-page touchpoint (custom Pre-commit/Pre-push/Pre-receive messages surface via ggshield) so a tester who configured a different tab is not misled.

assertions.text: Does NOT emit 'custom workflow', 'custom remediation workflow configured', 'configured by your workspace', or any equivalent claim — because no id is present
Identifies the returned workflow as GitGuardian's default (no id), and still lets the doctrine drive the remediation
Notes (or does not contradict) that get_remediation_workflow returns only the Incident-page touchpoint; custom Pre-commit/Pre-push/Pre-receive messages surface via ggshield, not here
